warnings: Flu vaccine effectiveness is NOT a fixed number: the commonly-quoted 40-60% figure applies to well-matched seasons. The just-completed 2025-26 season was a lower-effectiveness, mismatched season (~22% vs outpatient illness, ~30% vs hospitalization in adults, per CDC's preliminary VE page dated 2026-03-16). The game should frame VE as a range that varies by season, not a constant, or it will read as wrong within a year.

Flu burden numbers (illnesses/hospitalizations/deaths) are season-specific and CDC republishes them annually. The most recent finalized full-season CDC estimate available today is for 2024-25 (51M illnesses / 710K hospitalizations / 45K deaths); CDC had stopped posting in-season 2025-26 estimates for the summer as of the pages checked and had not yet posted a finalized 2025-26 season summary comparable to the 2024-25 one. Plan to refresh this claim once the 2025-26 final summary posts and again for 2026-27.

Could not verify a specific 'X% of adults fear/avoid needles' statistic on any live cdc.gov page (only found on aggregator/blog sites attributing it loosely to CDC or ACIP) -- omitted rather than inventing a number. The needle-anxiety coping tips themselves ARE from a current CDC page.

Could not find a current, non-archived cdc.gov page that explicitly states it's 'still worth it' / 'not too late' to get vaccinated in December/January. That messaging exists only in archived National Influenza Vaccination Week campaign material from 2011-2016 (stacks.cdc.gov / archive.cdc.gov). The underlying two-week-immunity logic supports the point, but don't attribute the 'not too late' phrase itself to a current CDC page.

Tdap 'cocooning' (vaccinating adults/teens around a newborn) is supported by a current, dedicated CDC page (vaccines-pregnancy/about/vaccines-family-caregivers.html, updated 2024-06-05), but CDC's main current Pertussis Vaccination Recommendations page (updated 2025-12-02) does not restate this cocooning language for adult close contacts -- it only covers pregnancy and adolescent/adult primary dosing. Both pages are live; this looks like an emphasis difference across pages rather than a retraction, but flag for re-check.

No CDC page found gives a Shingrix (RZV)-specific effectiveness percentage (e.g., '>90% effective'); the only efficacy numbers on CDC's shingles HCP page are for the older Zostavax vaccine. Do not use a '90%+' Shingrix effectiveness stat without a live CDC citation -- use the '1 in 3 lifetime risk' statistic instead, which IS CDC-sourced.

Pneumococcal age threshold changed from 65 to 50 in October 2024 (ACIP) -- if any existing game content still says 'age 65' for pneumococcal, that is now wrong per the current CDC recommendations page (updated 2026-02-25).

The pneumococcal burden statistic (150,000+ hospitalizations/year) is from CDC's Pink Book chapter (updated 2024-04-19), which itself draws on older underlying epidemiologic estimates (the page's invasive-disease case/death numbers are explicitly from 2017). Treat it as an order-of-magnitude figure, not a current-year number.

None of the cdc.gov pages fetched for this research were blocked; all fetches succeeded. restoredcdc.org (an unofficial third-party mirror of archived/removed CDC pages) appeared in several search results but was never used as a cited source -- only live cdc.gov pages were cited.

All URLs and quotes above were fetched fresh today (2026-09-15) via WebFetch; several pages' stated 'Updated' dates are very recent (some as late as September 2026), consistent with CDC's routine seasonal refresh cycle -- re-verify again before each new flu season if this ledger is reused.
